content.content:
# Cloud Agent Builds: Install Timing & Persistence

## When Install Runs

The `install` command executes "During each Build" and is meant for "Installing dependencies, generating code, compiling artifacts, and warming disk caches."

## What Persists from Build to Agent

Builds preserve the prepared disk state. When an agent starts from an active Build, it receives the machine with repositories cloned, dependencies installed, and caches warmed. This means installed binaries, compiled artifacts, and cached packages from the install phase are available to the agent.

## What Does NOT Persist

Critically, "Builds preserve disk state only. Running processes, shell exports, and in-memory caches stop when Cursor snapshots the machine." This means environment variables set during installation, shell configurations, and any running processes are lost. Services must be started via the `start` or `terminals` commands instead.

## Snapshot & Caching Decision Logic

Cursor skips recurring Builds when "nothing changed since the last completed one: no new commits on the default branch of any repository in the environment, and no configuration or secret changes." If the Build remains active and hasn't crossed the staleness threshold, agents reuse it as-is. However, if "Update stale builds" is enabled and the Build exceeds the threshold, agents will pull fresh code at startup while keeping the cached dependencies.

That's the trap, precisely. Line 6: `DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin"`, used at line 239 with **no override flag or env var**, and lines 315-325 just *print* PATH instructions for a human to paste. Meanwhile Cursor's docs say exported shell variables don't survive into the agent run — and Entire's Cursor hooks use the silent wrapper, so a missing `entire` means every hook no-ops with no error.

cd /Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/soph-cursor-feedback
cat > .cursor/install-entire.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Make the Entire CLI available to Cursor cloud agents.
#
# Why this is needed at all
# -------------------------
# .cursor/hooks.json is committed, so a cloud agent DOES fire Entire's hooks.
# But each one is wrapped as:
#
#   sh -c 'if ! command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 0; fi; exec entire hooks cursor ...'
#
# A missing binary therefore makes every hook a silent no-op — no error, no log
# line, and `entire status` still looks healthy. Cloud VMs have no entire
# installed, so without this script a cloud agent's whole session is dropped
# silently.
#
# Why a symlink and not a PATH export
# -----------------------------------
# Cursor's docs: a Build "preserves disk state only ... exported shell variables
# don't continue into an agent run." So `export PATH=...` here would not survive
# to hook-exec time. install.sh hardcodes DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin"
# with no flag or env override, and only *prints* PATH instructions for a human
# to paste. We link the binary into a directory already on the default PATH,
# which persists because it is disk state.
#
# Idempotent by requirement: Cursor runs install for every Build and may run it
# on previously prepared disk state.
#
# Best-effort by design: this never fails the Build. A broken capture setup must
# not stop the agent from doing the user's actual work. To make it fatal
# instead, change the final `exit 0` to `exit 1`.

set -uo pipefail

log() { printf '[entire-setup] %s\n' "$*"; }

# Only act where this repo actually opted into Entire.
if [ ! -f .entire/settings.json ] && [ ! -f .entire/settings.local.json ]; then
  log "no .entire settings — Entire not enabled here, nothing to do"
  exit 0
fi

LINK_DIR=/usr/local/bin

link_into_path() {
  # $1 = binary name. Links ~/.local/bin/$1 into a dir on the default PATH.
  local name="$1" src="$HOME/.local/bin/$1"
  [ -x "$src" ] || return 0
  [ -e "$LINK_DIR/$name" ] && return 0
  if [ -w "$LINK_DIR" ]; then
    ln -sf "$src" "$LINK_DIR/$name"
  elif command -v sudo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    sudo ln -sf "$src" "$LINK_DIR/$name" 2>/dev/null || log "could not link $name into $LINK_DIR"
  else
    log "cannot write $LINK_DIR and no sudo; $name may be unreachable from hooks"
  fi
}

if ! command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing Entire CLI (stable)..."
  # Switch to nightly with: bash -s -- --channel nightly
  curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || log "installer exited non-zero"
fi

link_into_path entire
# git-remote-entire ships alongside and is what resolves `git clone entire://…`.
link_into_path git-remote-entire

if ! command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "WARNING: entire is still not on PATH."
  log "WARNING: Cursor hooks will silently no-op and this agent's session will NOT be captured."
  exit 0
fi

log "using $(command -v entire) — $(entire --version 2>/dev/null | head -1)"

# .git/hooks is per-clone and never committed, so a fresh cloud clone has none.
# Without prepare-commit-msg there is no Entire-Checkpoint trailer, and PostCommit
# returns early when the trailer is absent — so commits produce no checkpoint even
# though the agent hooks fired. doctor --force reinstalls them: it is
# content-idempotent, backs up any foreign hook, and self-gates on
# settings.IsSetUpAny, so it stays a no-op in a repo that never opted in.
entire doctor --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "doctor --force reported problems (continuing)"
entire doctor 2>&1 | grep -iE "git hooks" || log "could not confirm git hook state"

exit 0
EOF
chmod +x .cursor/install-entire.sh
echo "written .cursor/install-entire.sh ($(wc -l < .cursor/install-entire.sh) lines)"
bash -n .cursor/install-entire.sh && echo "syntax OK"

content.text:
Yes — Cursor has exactly the hook for this: **`.cursor/environment.json`** with an `install` script. I wrote both files (uncommitted, and sitting on the `soph/e2e-cursor-timeout` branch — I'd move them to their own branch before committing).

## The two things that make it non-trivial

**1. Installing the binary isn't enough.** Cursor's docs are explicit that a Build "preserves disk state only … exported shell variables don't continue into an agent run." And `install.sh` line 6 hardcodes `DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin"` with no flag or env override — it only *prints* PATH instructions for a human to paste. So `curl … | bash` plus a `PATH` export would install the binary and still leave every hook dead, because the wrapper is `if ! command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 0; fi`. Silent no-op, no log, `entire status` green. The script therefore symlinks into `/usr/local/bin`, which is on the default PATH and persists as disk state.

**2. Git hooks are the half that's easy to miss.** `.cursor/hooks.json` is committed, so agent hooks fire in cloud. `.git/hooks` is per-clone and never committed, so a fresh cloud clone has **none** — no `prepare-commit-msg`, no `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, and `PostCommit` returns early without one. The agent hooks would fire and still produce zero checkpoints. `entire doctor --force` fixes that: content-idempotent, backs up foreign hooks, non-interactive-safe by design, and it self-gates on `settings.IsSetUpAny` — so it's literally "only when Entire is enabled," which is what you asked for.

## Files

`.cursor/environment.json` (JSONC — the schema sets `allowComments`):

```jsonc
{ "install": "bash .cursor/install-entire.sh" }
```

`.cursor/install-entire.sh` — gates on `.entire/settings.json`, installs only if `entire` is missing, symlinks into a PATH dir (with `sudo` fallback and a graceful give-up), then runs `doctor --force` and echoes the git-hook state. Idempotent, and **always exits 0** so a capture problem never blocks the agent's real work; one-line comment says how to make it fatal.

Smoke-tested locally: skips install, skips linking (already on PATH), reports `✓ Git hooks: OK`.

## Two things for you to decide

**Merge, don't replace.** You said Cursor is setting up dependencies right now — its agent-led setup will likely write its own `environment.json`, and there can only be one. When it does, chain into its `install` rather than keeping my file; the comment in the file shows the pattern. I put Entire first deliberately, since it always exits 0, so capture survives a failing dependency step.

**Channel.** I defaulted to stable. This file is committed and affects every teammate's cloud agents, so a nightly regression in the hook path would hit all of them — but this being Entire's own repo, you may want nightly for dogfooding. One-word change, flagged in a comment.

Worth knowing about the result: cloud agents fire `beforeSubmitPrompt` and `stop` — the pair that creates session state and mints checkpoints — but **not** `sessionStart`/`sessionEnd` ("deferred while cloud agents can still start in a read-only environment"). So capture should work, but sessions will never get a clean end and will rely on the stuck-active timeout, since cross-host liveness reads as Unknown. No Entire login needed: checkpoint refs ride along on the agent's own `git push` via the pre-push hook.

Want me to commit these on their own branch and open a third PR? I'd hold until Cursor finishes generating its environment file, so we write one merged version instead of fighting over the filename.

Two bot reviews on #2112, both flagging the same line — my `initGitRepo` setting `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` to `/dev/null`. No human reviews yet; `REVIEW_REQUIRED`.

**They disagreed on the fix, and Bugbot was closer.** Copilot said use `os.DevNull` (`NUL` on Windows); Bugbot said `NUL` also fails for git config and the repo already isolates via a real file. Checking, Bugbot's pattern claim holds — `gitrepo/reftable_test.go:36` uses `filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "gitconfig")`. Git treats a missing config file as empty, so a real path isolates just as well and is portable.

**But both got the severity wrong.** Bugbot filed it Medium, asserting "these new DetectPresence tests fail on a full Windows run." That can't happen in this repo. `ci.yml:70` runs Windows as:

```
go test ./cmd/entire/cli/... -run '(Windows|MSYS)'
```

with the workflow comment explaining why: *"Real-Windows tests must include Windows or MSYS in their top-level test name so this job selects them without running POSIX-only harnesses."* No `TestDetectPresence_*` name matches, so they never execute on Windows CI. It's a portability nit that would only bite someone running the full suite locally on Windows — real, but not a bug and not a CI risk.

Also worth noting against Bugbot's "the repo already documents this pitfall": the convention is only half-followed. `reftable_test.go` gives `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` a temp path but passes `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null` on the very next line. So my code matched existing precedent as much as it broke it.

Applied anyway — the portable form costs nothing and reads better. Both vars now point into a temp dir, which is strictly better than the existing convention. Pushed as `a5aa8656f`; lint clean, agent tree green.
